review_note:
REVIEWED AND APPROVED by Joe 2026-07-31 (structure-only: producing a real grid waits on premises records, Wave 3).

PROPOSED map, not reviewed. The grid is a REPEATING shape: four property column-pairs, each carrying a frozen OFFERED column and a live CURRENT column over twenty deal points. That is one negotiation_round per property per side, keyed to a premises — so the map declares the addressing in full and resolves it as a unit, rather than pretending 160 independent slots exist.

SENDABLE FORMAT (Joe's doctrine, 2026-07-31, superseding the old blanket 'clients get PDFs, never working files'): this is a SPREADSHEET template, so the PDF is the sendable artifact and the working workbook never leaves. Concealing the formulas is the whole point. Naming a sendable format is not itself an ask to send: it goes out when Joe asks (decision 41906a30).

title.label: Title
title.owed_note: Client display name and the run date. HYPHENS, not the template placeholder's em-dashes: writing-rules hard-bans the em-dash on every surface a prospect could see, and the factory's own output must not be the thing that trips its own gate. The template's remaining em-dashes (A2, the four PROPERTY headers, A14, A27) are Joe's to rule on.

repeat.name: properties
repeat.label: The four property column-pairs (OFFERED frozen / CURRENT live)

16.label: Est. build-out cost ($/SF)
16.owed_note: No record field: build-out cost is the tenant's own estimate, not a negotiated term. Belongs to the comparison workbook.

17.label: TI gap
17.owed_note: Derived from row 15 minus row 16; the template computes it once both are present.

19.label: Purchase option
19.owed_note: Shares options_note with row 18 today — one text column carrying two different facts. Splitting it is a schema question, flagged not improvised.

24.label: Effective total cost
24.owed_note: Comes from the lease-comparison workbook, not the record layer. Cross-document, deliberately left to the human.

repeat.owed_note: Needs (1) premises rows for the candidate properties and (2) negotiation_round rows per premises for the OFFERED (round 1) and CURRENT (newest) columns. The record layer holds zero premises and zero spaces today, so this block resolves as one owed entry until a space search is recorded.
